objections.claim: The branch-publisher principal is specified as `contents:write ONLY`, yet it must open pull requests; GitHub's create-pull-request operation requires pull-request write permission. The stated credential therefore cannot perform the proposed workflow. Granting the missing permission changes the custody manifest and live-scope oracle, so the approach must reconcile and test the actual least-privilege permission set.

The substituted-definition defense is fail-open. A non-main workflow can request a write-scoped GITHUB_TOKEN; the repository's read-only default is not a permission ceiling, and an environment policy gates environment credentials, not GITHUB_TOKEN. Such a run can perform repository mutations and can invoke the merge endpoint for a branch-protection-eligible PR without the controller-only Eye-acceptance check. It can also mutate an unpublished draft release. The v* tag ruleset and attestation identity do not prevent those operations, while the closed custody manifest does not account for this ephemeral Actions writer. A platform-enforced ceiling or an architecture that makes Actions tokens incapable of these mutations is required.

The input-history freshness mechanism is not preserved across the proposed merge operation. The snapshot binds path-history commit identities at the PR head, but `PUT .../merge` does not pin or verify a history-preserving merge method, and the required check is expressly run against the PR-head checkout rather than the exact post-merge history. A squash, rebase, or otherwise different server-produced topology can therefore make the newly merged main immediately fail `input-history-stale`, violating the atomic-weave invariant. The controller must constrain and verify the merge strategy and test the resulting main topology, or derive eligibility against the exact history that will exist after mutation.
